# Appeal of Denial — Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446)

**Member:** Quinn Ellison
**Member ID:** W391580594
**Payer/Plan:** Aetna (Commercial/ACA), Montana
**Reference Number:** POC-DF42BEB029-97975
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-04
**Governing Policy:** Aetna CPB 0660 - Knee Arthroplasty (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0660.html)

---

Dear Aetna Appeals Review Team,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for my partial knee replacement surgery (CPT 27446), as stated in the notice dated 2026-08-04, reference number POC-DF42BEB029-97975. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for me, and I am asking Aetna to reconsider this decision.

The denial letter states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I believe this conclusion does not match my own medical records or Aetna's own published criteria for this surgery, as set out in Aetna CPB 0660 - Knee Arthroplasty.

## Why I believe my records meet Aetna's own criteria

**1. Single compartment involvement.**
Aetna's policy states that "unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) is indicated when only 1 compartment is affected, and total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is indicated when 2 or 3 compartments are affected."

My MRI from 2026-05-28 shows full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes limited to the medial compartment. This is the exact single-compartment pattern the policy describes as appropriate for UKA rather than TKA.

**2. Meeting the specific medical necessity criteria for UKA.**
The policy states that "Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty using Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved devices is considered medically necessary for members with advanced osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee affecting only a single compartment (medial, lateral or patellofemoral), and who meet the following criteria."

My records show advanced, single-compartment (medial) osteoarthritis, consistent with this description. [Placeholder: confirm the specific FDA-approved device/prosthesis proposed by Dr. Lindqvist, if required for this criterion.]

**3. History of unsuccessful conservative therapy.**
The policy requires "History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management)" and specifies that "Members with osteoarthritis, traumatic arthritis, or avascular necrosis should have at least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record ... with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy) in the past year."

My records document 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy (24 visits) from 2026-02-25 to 2026-06-17, focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, along with 8 months of NSAID use and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-02 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief. This meets and exceeds the 12-week minimum, with formal in-person physical therapy as the plan requires.

**4. Severity supporting surgical treatment.**
The policy notes that "Conservative therapy may be inappropriate for severe osteoarthritis with bone-on-bone articulation in the weight-bearing portion of the joint (medial and/or lateral but not patello-femoral)" and that "If conservative therapy is not appropriate, the medical record must clearly document why such approach is not reasonable."

My MRI documents bone-on-bone apposition in the medial compartment, which is the weight-bearing portion of the joint. Despite this, I completed a full course of conservative treatment as described above, and my symptoms have continued to progress — I have 18 months of progressive pain unrelieved by rest, I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake 3-4 times nightly from pain.

## My current condition

For context, my records also show:
- No active infection
- No untreated substance use
- BMI of 29
- Non-smoker
- Positive provocative testing on the affected side and pain-limited range of motion on exam

I have not found anything in these records suggesting any of the absolute contraindications described in Aetna's policy, but I understand Aetna's reviewers have access to my full chart and will confirm this.

## What I am asking

I am asking Aetna to reconsider this denial in light of my surgeon's documentation and the medical records described above, which I believe meet Aetna's own published criteria for unicompartmental knee arthroplasty under CPB 0660. I am not asking for a guarantee of approval — only a full review of my records against the plan's own stated criteria.

Please let me know if any additional records, forms, or information are needed to complete this appeal. I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-01-31, and I am submitting it accordingly. I will confirm the correct appeal mailing/fax address printed on my denial letter, and will also submit through the Member Complaint and Appeal Form in my Aetna online account, by fax to 859-425-3379, or by phone at 1-800-872-3862 if needed.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Quinn Ellison
Member ID: W391580594
[Phone number]
[Mailing address]
[Date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
